corrected_verdict: PARTIALLY_KNOWN, with a correctness caveat. The template is Morwani App. F.1 (Plancherel + AM-GM + Cauchy-Schwarz, quadratic neuron only). The Lipschitz variance contraction is textbook. No prior ReLU single-neuron budget was found. However, the stated constant p/4 and C_2 <= p^{-n}/2 are false for n>=2: the correct values are p^n/4 and C_2 <= 1/(2p).
issues: (1) The checker's j=0 concern does not apply. prelim.tex defines \Fp={1,...,(p-1)/2}, so j=0 is already excluded, and recommended change 2 is unnecessary. (2) The checker missed an error in the constant (appendix.tex l.283). With the paper's unnormalised DFT, Parseval on Z_p^n gives sum_{j in Fp}|h^(j..j)|^2 <= (1/2)p^{2n}Var(h) <= (1/2)p^{2n-1}sum_t||u_t||^2. The bound is therefore sum_{j in Fp}|h^(j..j)w^(j)| <= (p^n/4)||omega||^2, not (p/4)||omega||^2, and C_2 <= 1/(2p), not p^{-n}/2. The two agree only at n=1. A numerical check at n=2 (script saved as relu_budget_check.py in the item folder) finds ratios of 5.8, 25.3 and 105 at p=11, 23 and 47, against a claimed p/4 of 2.75, 5.75 and 11.75. The qualitative claim (b=nu=2 endpoint, flat maximizer) survives; the constant must be fixed. (3) Both confirmed citations check out verbatim. Morwani 2311.07568v2 App. F.1 (Theorem 7) has the Plancherel, AM-GM and Cauchy-Schwarz steps and 'shifting the mean of w does not affect the margin'; its ReLU content is experiments only. Gromov 2301.02679 says 'The weights (6)-(7) also work for other activation functions, including ReLU' (empirical). (4) Search caveat: the session WebSearch budget was exhausted (200/200) on this task's first query, so the independent novelty search was limited to the fetched PDFs. This budget exhaustion, plus WebFetch returning unreadable binary for arXiv PDFs (each verifier then needs extra pdftotext rounds), is a likely cause of the slow verify stage.
